title: Mopane Airlines

sentences.text: You are a strategy consultant appointed by Mopane's board.
Mopane Airlines (Pty) Ltd flies regional routes from Lanseria to five towns in Limpopo and Mpumalanga.
It was founded in 1998 by two former air force pilots, who still sit on the board.
Mopane holds the only licence to fly scheduled flights into Hoedspruit until 2029.
Its on-time rate of 91% is the best of any South African regional airline.
Two of its six aircraft are more than 25 years old and were out of service for 40 days last year.
For the year ended 30 June 2026 Mopane made a loss of R38 million, its third loss in a row.
Current liabilities exceed current assets by R64 million.
A R120 million bank loan must be repaid in full in March 2027, and the bank has said it will not extend it.
Jet fuel makes up 35% of operating costs and is priced in US dollars.
The board is considering selling two aircraft and leasing them back, merging with a larger airline, or raising R80 million from a new shareholder.
Tourist arrivals in the Kruger area grew 14% in 2025, and two new lodges near Hoedspruit open in 2027.
A low-cost airline has announced that it will start flying to Mbombela in 2027.
Two mining companies have asked Mopane to quote for weekly charter flights to their sites.

required: Prepare a SWOT analysis for Mopane Airlines in view of its going concern challenges. Do not discuss the board proposals in paragraph 3.

recall.question: What kind of business is Mopane?
options: A regional airline in financial difficulty
A national airline expanding abroad
An aircraft leasing company
A tourism lodge operator

recall.question: What is your role?
options: A strategy consultant advising the board
Mopane's external auditor
A credit analyst at the bank
Mopane's financial manager

recall.question: What is the main issue running through the case?
options: Whether Mopane can survive: losses, and a loan it cannot repay
A breach of ethics by the directors
A dispute with the aviation regulator
A planned listing on the JSE

recall.question: What is the board considering?
options: Ways to raise money or restructure
Closing the airline
Buying new aircraft
Starting international routes
A SWOT: internal strengths and weaknesses, external opportunities and threats, each taken from the case
A discussion of whether Mopane is a going concern, ending in a conclusion
A recommendation on which board proposal to accept
A general list of strengths and weaknesses of regional airlines
shape.why: 'Prepare a SWOT' sets the form: four headings, internal and external, and every point taken from Mopane's own facts.

options.text: Leave out the board proposals in paragraph 3
Cover both the internal and the external environment
Use Mopane's own facts, not airlines in general

directions.why: The exclusion is the one students miss: a sale and leaseback or new capital looks like an opportunity, but paragraph 3 is out of bounds.

options: How each point affects Mopane's ability to keep going: cash, the loan, the losses
How each point affects passengers
Whether the directors acted ethically
How each point affects the audit opinion
lens.why: 'In view of its going concern challenges' is the angle. A strength or opportunity only counts when you show how it helps Mopane survive.

rows.point: Strength: the only scheduled licence into Hoedspruit until 2029 protects a route and its income
Strength: the best on-time rate (91%) supports customer loyalty and revenue
Weakness: an ageing fleet; 40 days out of service cuts capacity and income
Weakness: a third loss in a row (R38 million) drains cash and equity
Weakness: net current liabilities of R64 million, so short-term debts cannot be met from current assets
Weakness or threat: the R120 million loan is due in March 2027 with no extension, so without new funding Mopane may not be able to repay it (significant doubt about going concern)
Threat: fuel is 35% of costs and priced in dollars, so a weaker rand raises costs and deepens losses
Opportunity: tourism growth and new lodges near Hoedspruit, where Mopane holds the only licence, bring more passengers and cash
Threat: a low-cost airline flying to Mbombela from 2027 will put pressure on fares and income
Opportunity: charter contracts with the mines would bring regular, contracted income that eases cash flow
